storySection.title: A Packaging Story of Love & Innovation
paragraphs: Valentine’s season is one of the most competitive times for brands to win hearts and stand out. KitKat India wanted to ‘own’ the season with something innovative that tied seamlessly into its iconic brand line: ‘Have a Break, Have a KitKat.’ The challenge was to connect love with the break narrative in a fresh, memorable way.
This was not just about creating a wrapper — it was about crafting a brand packaging design that would become a cultural moment.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.description: For Valentine’s season, KitKat aimed to create a campaign that resonated with young audiences and reinforced its playful brand persona.

list.text: The goal was to own the Valentine’s moment in India.
Go beyond the core message “Have a Break, Have a Kit Kat” into a love-themed concept.
Mix “breaks” with “love” in a new, relatable way for Gen Z and millennials.
Differentiate among the cacophony of festive noise but without becoming risque or making the light, witty tone too far away from the spirit of KitKat.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: One concept emerged immediately in brainstorming: 'Love Break.'

list.description: Love is emotional, personal, and individualized, much like each relationship. What if the package itself told that story of being individualized? Rather than one single design, we saw custom packaging designs that honored individuality.

With HP Mosaic and Collage Digital Printing technology, we produced thousands of individual packs, each with its own unique appearance and message. The imagery featured millennial slang acronyms, fun motifs, and bright colors, all appealing to the young KitKat consumer.
This wasn't food packaging design; this was innovative packaging design that combined technology and imagination and transformed a chocolate bar into a gift.

executionSection.title: The Creative Execution
executionSection.description: Product Packaging Design: Each wrapper was crafted to feel fresh and collectible, using bold typography and millennial symbols.

list.title: Brand Packaging Design
list.description: Every element tied back to KitKat’s essence of sharing breaks, now reimagined around sharing love.

list.title: Package Logo Design & Labelling
list.description: The familiar KitKat identity remained central, surrounded by playful, love-centric graphics.

list.title: Retail Packaging Design
list.description: Packs were optimized for shelf impact — instantly recognizable and attractive during the Valentine’s rush.

list.title: Luxury Packaging Design Touch
list.description: Unique packs elevated KitKat from a simple treat to a thoughtful, gift-ready product.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The “Love Break” packaging wasn’t just a campaign; it was a phenomenon. Each package design felt like a personal token, encouraging fans to gift KitKat to their loved ones.

list.text: Thousands of unique packs were rolled out across India, with no two designs alike.
Social media buzz skyrocketed as users shared photos of their personalized KitKat wrappers.
Retailers reported high shelf movement, making it one of the most successful Valentine’s pushes.
The campaign reinforced KitKat’s connection with youth culture through fun, emotional, and shareable packaging design services.

whySection.description: This case study demonstrates how thoughtful packaging design can turn a wrapper into an emotional experience — merging creativity, technology, and storytelling.

storySection.title: A Sophisticated Design Challenge
paragraphs: When 100 Pipers came to us, the challenge was daring: produce a Limited Edition pack that would break through the noise, communicate sophistication, and make an impact. They needed something sleek, elegant, and visually distinctive — packaging that would transform the brand in a crowded shelf environment.
This wasn’t simply about building another wrapper — it was about creating a packaging design for a brand that would be seen as a work of art.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.description: 100 Pipers wanted to up its brand ante in a competitive market and connect better with its audience.

list.text: The brand was struggling to establish a distinctive position in the crowded spirits market.
It wanted a brand campaign which could appeal emotionally and culturally to its target adult segment.
There was a need to position 100 Pipers distinctively against other high-end blends, more-so in India by highlighting its heritage as well as contemporary positioning.
In addition, the campaign needed to be adaptable to various formats and platforms and comply with alcohol advertising regulations.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: We wanted the pack itself to become an experience. So, we adopted a post-modern Deconstructivist art style — deconstructing the iconic Piper figure and reconstructing it across the bottle series. Each bottle became a fragment of a larger visual story. When placed side-by-side, the design completed itself.

list.title: Innovative Packaging Design
list.description: The fragmented visual across bottles created intrigue — the full image was revealed only in collective display.

list.title: Retail Packaging Design Flair
list.description: On shelves, the range enticed consumers to collect, compare, and engage visually.

list.title: Custom Packaging Design Artistry
list.description: Each bottle maintained visual individuality while contributing to the larger artistic composition.

list.title: Brand Packaging Consistency
list.description: Despite the fragmentation, the Piper motif and brand DNA remained recognizable and intact.

executionSection.title: The Creative Execution
executionSection.description: Package label design & graphic layout: We structured each label fragment so that lines, shapes, and negatives aligned seamlessly.

list.title: Structural design coordination
list.description: Working with bottling partners to ensure the deconstructed art aligned properly across cylindrical surfaces.

list.title: Premium finish & print execution
list.description: High-contrast colors, crisp lines, and premium print finishes gave the pack luxury appeal.

list.title: Range strategy
list.description: The complete visual was only visible when the full range was displayed side by side, enhancing collectability and shelf storytelling.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The Limited Edition 100 Pipers packaging became a retail standout — a fine balance of design, art, and brand storytelling.

list.text: High shelf visibility — the fragmented art triggered second glances and buzz.
Increased brand prestige — the packaging elevated the product perception.
Social and visual appeal — consumers shared and discussed the art-inspired bottles.
Positive client feedback — the brand acknowledged that we didn’t just meet expectations, we exceeded them.

list.text: How custom packaging design can create emotional resonance

storySection.title: A Festive Story That Illuminated Hearts
paragraphs: For Indians living abroad, Diwali is more than a festival, it’s a feeling of home. Nestlé wanted to capture that emotion for its Quality Street range in Canada, turning a box of chocolates into something that would spark nostalgia, pride, and joy.

The brief to us at Prakria was exciting and demanding: design a packaging concept that honored tradition but felt modern, premium, and gift-worthy. Not just food packaging design is something people would want to keep on the table even after the last chocolate was eaten.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.description: To really capture the Canadian Indian & Asian diaspora for Quality Street at Diwali, Quality Street had to be relevant and striking.

list.text: The audience was the Indians in Canada, who are deeply attached to home and festivals.
The brand had to create a communication that was both in tune with traditional Diwali sensibilities and disruptive in terms of execution.
Their ask was for a limited-edition pack design that felt premium, collectible, and relevant beyond just the festival period.
The design needed to present a coexistence of the down to earth (traditional) and the heightened (innovative packaging).

challenge.subDescription: In other words, the task was to take a celebratory pack and turn it into a cultural keepsake that made an emotional connection with the diaspora, that also had a premium look and feel and standout design.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: When we thought about Diwali, one image kept coming back, the Diya, glowing softly in The Strategy. Our vision was to make the Diwali gifting experience as special as the festival itself. The inspiration came from the humble Diya, a timeless symbol of light, warmth, and celebration.

list.title: Creative Concept
list.description: We reimagined the iconic Quality Street pack into the shape of a Diya. The design wasn’t just aesthetic, it carried cultural meaning, connecting instantly with the spirit of Diwali.

list.title: Design Detailing
list.description:
Every element of the packaging was thoughtfully crafted:

- The folds and contours of the box mirrored the flame of a Diya.
- The color palette and finishes evoked festivity without falling into cliché.
- The label design beautifully balanced Nestlé’s branding with traditional motifs.

list.title: Experience Design
list.description: Inside, the chocolates were arranged like a treasure, making the unboxing feel like opening a festive gift. Every layer was designed to delight, from the first glance to the final bite.

list.title: Outcome
list.description: The result? A limited edition pack that looked more like décor than packaging, perfect for gifting, sharing, and cherishing.

executionSection.title: The Creative Execution
executionSection.description: A special edition pack was designed with festive spirit: elaborate gold foiling, rich jewel-tones – particularly purple – and a premium tin packaging that added a touch of luxury to the product for gifting during Diwali.

list.title: Focus on differentiator
list.description: packaging popped on shelf -higher-end material, celebratory cues, and a diaspora-specific framing (celebrating abroad, maintaining roots) lending the brand a particularly strong seasonal pull. Creative Execution

list.title: The limited-edition pack was made in a festive special
list.description: rich gold foiling, deep jewel-tones (especially purple) and premium tin packaging that took the product to a level for Diwali gifting.

list.title: The design worked on a cultural level
list.description: Patterns and colour references to Indian festive aesthetics (for the diaspora market) were incorporated, while maintaining the brand’s heritage. The pack and communication adopted a “keepsake” mindset—the tin is positioned not just as a chocolate box, but as a collectible or memento for the festival season.

list.title: Integrated across touch-points
list.description:
Social media teasers, influencer un-boxing videos, in-store displays and POS that reinforced “celebration”, “heritage” and “gift-worthiness”.

Messaging leveraged the brand’s iconic legacy (wrappers, characters) but with a modern twist: suggesting “share the joy”, “make this Diwali a moment” and “a tradition re-imagined”.

list.title: Attention to differentiator
list.description: packaging stood out on shelf,  premium material, festive cues, and a diaspora-specific framing (celebration abroad, staying connected with roots) giving the brand a strong seasonal pull.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The response was overwhelming. For the Indian diaspora in Canada, the pack became more than a treat — it was a reminder of home. Families displayed it proudly during celebrations, while shoppers picked it up not just for chocolates but for its design. Retailers reported rapid sell-outs, and the campaign created buzz across communities. The design extended the product’s life well beyond the holiday, strengthening Quality Street’s visibility and emotional connection.

list.text: High emotional resonance among the Indian diaspora community.
Retailers saw increased off-shelf pickup and social media buzz.
The pack was often repurposed as décor — extending product value.
Quality Street’s brand perception elevated from festive treat to heartfelt gift.

storySection.title: The Concept — A Break at Your Desk
paragraphs: As work moved out of offices and into homes, our desks became all-day destinations. With back-to-back calls and endless to-do lists, everyone was in need of little pick-me-ups to keep the day going. Perfetti noticed this shift and wondered — what if we could give people a little joy, right at their desks?

That’s how the concept of the Workdesk Pack came to life — a convenient combination of favorite treats, designed especially for home-office life. To bring this idea to reality, Perfetti partnered with Prakria to create a pack that was practical, delightful, and perfectly timed for the new normal.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.description: With the move to remote working and “work from home” routines during/after lockdowns, working professionals were looking for easily-accessible refreshment options at their desks.

list.text: Perfetti identified this shift as an opportunity: they needed to design a pack tailored for the work-desk environment, not just a regular retail pack.
The brand wanted to launch this “Work Desk Pack” primarily via digital channels, so speed, digital-readiness, and eye-catching design were all critical.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: Our goal was to align product innovation with a rapidly changing lifestyle, the work-from-home routine. The concept was aptly named “Work Desk Pack” to immediately communicate its purpose and utility.

list.title: Creative Concept
list.description: We designed a snack-pack that complemented the work desk environment,  compact, accessible, and tailored for quick refreshment during busy workdays.

list.title: Design Detailing
list.description: The packaging design reflected fun, refreshment, and enjoyment,  the core ethos of Perfetti. At the same time, it was shaped for functionality, making it convenient to keep and use on a desk without clutter.

list.title: Speed to Market
list.description: Leveraging agility, PRAKRIA and Perfetti executed the design and digital launch cycle at remarkable speed. This rapid turnaround helped the brand stay ahead of the curve, capturing the new market behaviour early and effectively.

list.title: Outcome
list.description: The result was a product-pack that blended design thinking with timely relevance,  a perfect example of creativity meeting consumer insight in real time.

executionSection.title: The Creative Execution
executionSection.description: We asked ourselves: If a pack is going to sit on someone’s desk all day, what should it feel like? The answer: bright enough to lift your mood, compact enough to fit anywhere, and fun enough to make you smile.

list.title: Naming the Pack
list.description: We kept it simple and clear - “Workdesk Pack.” It says exactly what it is and makes it instantly relatable.

list.title: Creative Package Design
list.description: The look combined bold, cheerful colors with clean lines, making it stand out on both physical and digital shelves.

list.title: Package Label Design
list.description: Strong typography and playful product cues gave the pack a friendly yet professional vibe.

list.title: Practicality First
list.description: The structure was compact so it could fit neatly on a desk, always within reach for a quick treat.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The launch was a hit. People loved the idea of having a pack that was made for their new routines. It wasn’t just another box of candy, it was a thoughtful little desk companion.Quick Market Response: By acting fast, Perfetti got ahead of the curve and grabbed attention early.

list.text: Digital Appeal: The bright, relatable design made it perfect for online promotion, sparking social shares and conversations.
Brand Love: The pack reinforced Perfetti’s image as a brand that understands its audience and adapts to changing times.
Practical & Fun: It balanced utility with playfulness, showing how brand packaging design can be both smart and joyful.

whySection.description: The Perfetti Workdesk Pack is proof that great design doesn’t have to be complicated. Sometimes, it’s about reading the moment and responding with creativity.It's a custom packaging design built for a cultural shift.

storySection.title: The Story — Turning Everyday Moments into Escapes
paragraphs: Palmolive is known for its great products. But in a marketspace as cluttered as that of bathing products, finding a unique space was quite a challenge. They needed something that was beyond a mere ‘product’. They needed an experience.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.description: Palmolive, known globally for care products, wanted to go beyond the ordinary. They didn’t just want packaging — they wanted an experience. The brief was to make every unboxing moment feel like a mini holiday, blending visual indulgence with emotional resonance. The challenge was to make people pause, breathe, and experience calm in their everyday lives.

list.text: The goal was to transform the everyday shower into a moment of calm and self-care,  a brief escape from the busyness of daily life.
The challenge was to design packaging that evokes emotion and experience, not just shelf appeal.
The design needed to balance beauty and purpose, creating a sense of serenity while staying true to Palmolive’s identity.
In essence, the brief was simple yet ambitious: “Don’t just design packaging. Create an experience.”

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: Our aim was to transform a simple bath kit into a sensory ritual, something that evoked indulgence, calm, and escape. The concept was named “European Bathing Treasures” to capture the charm of Europe’s most luxurious spa traditions.

list.title: Creative Concept
list.description: We explored what makes a bath feel special: the scents, textures, and little details that create a ritual. The idea was to make every aspect of the experience,  from visuals to structure — feel soothing and transportive.

list.title: Design Detailing
list.description:
Refined, balanced fonts that felt premium yet approachable — evoking timeless European design cues.

Every element of the packaging was crafted to echo this European sensibility:

Soft, tranquil colors reminiscent of lavender fields and Mediterranean shores.

Elegant typography that conveyed premium quality while remaining warm and approachable.

A structural design that unfolded gracefully, making the unboxing feel like a moment of calm and care.

list.title: Experience Design
list.description: The kit wasn’t just about holding products; it created an emotional experience. The act of opening it became part of the ritual, turning daily bathing into something to look forward to.

executionSection.title: THE CREATIVE EXECUTION
executionSection.description: Research & Inspiration: We studied spa rituals, nature, and art from across Europe to create moodboards that captured relaxation and luxury.

list.title: Concept Development
list.description: Early sketches explored how the box could look and feel,  not just graphics, but the way it opened and held the bottles.

list.title: Design & Structure
list.description: We crafted a box that was sturdy, elegant, and gift-ready. The package label design and outer visuals worked seamlessly with the structure.

list.title: Finishing Touches
list.description: Soft-touch textures, subtle foiling, and premium materials gave it that luxury feel without being over the top.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: When the Palmolive European Treasures kit launched, the reaction was instant. Shoppers didn’t just see soap bottles, they saw a thoughtful kit they could display, gift, or keep for themselves.

list.text: The design made it stand out on digital platforms and retail shelves.
Reviews praised not only the product quality but the beauty of the packaging itself.
The brand felt elevated, moving from “everyday” to “premium.”
Most importantly, it made customers feel that a daily shower could be a little escape.

whySection.title: Why This Matters
whySection.description: This kit proved how powerful packaging design services can be: Custom packaging design can turn a routine product into something giftable.

list.text: Innovative packaging design can connect cultures and emotions.
